title: Characterization Facility, University of Minnesota
content:
The Characterization Facility (CharFac) is a shared analytical instrumentation facility in the College of Science and Engineering at the University of Minnesota, partially supported by the NSF through its MRSEC (DMR-2011401) and NNCI (ECCS-2025124) programs. It operates scanning and transmission electron microscopes, six scanning probe microscopes including Bruker AFM systems with PeakForce QNM, X-ray diffraction, elemental and chemical imaging, ion beam analysis, and optical and cryogenic microscopy, with staff providing training and full-service measurement.

Open to university researchers and external academic and industry clients on a fee-for-service basis, the CharFac gives aerogel and nanomaterials developers practical access to pore, surface and microstructure analysis, from morphology imaging to nanoscale mechanical mapping, without capital investment in instruments.
excerpt: University of Minnesota shared facility offering SEM/TEM, AFM, XRD and related materials characterization to academic and industry clients.
